papers.title: DRILL: Training World Models to Improve Policies, Not Predict Pixels
papers.abstract_snippet: World models are increasingly used to reduce environment interaction when post-training vision-language-action (VLA) policies with reinforcement learning. Yet they are typically trained to predict pixels one step ahead, even though their role here is not merely to render visually faithful videos but to produce learning signals from imagined rollouts that improve the policy. papers.title: A high-dimensional population code in the bat motor cortex during natural dexterous flight
papers.abstract_snippet: Bats use their hand-like wings to reproduce natural flights with wingbeat-level precision. Rather than mainly tracking the wingbeat cycle, the wing motor cortex generates sparse, distinct population states with little shared variance across wingbeats, resulting in a high-dimensional code distinct from that typically observed in constrained tasks.
papers.reason: 蝙蝠飞行时翼部运动皮层群体编码的神经科学研究，属系统神经科学，无机器人平台、无 VLA 或 embodied 控制实验，与机器人操作研究无实质关联。
